column1: # Which gate self-test a diff has to re-run, and which it does not.
# Read by .github/scripts/gate-self-tests.py. Every gate in this repository ships
# a self-test that mutates the gate, or the tree the gate reads, and requires the
# gate to redden -- a gate that is only known to pass is not known to detect.
# Those proofs used to run on every pull request, so a README typo paid for all
# of them and a diff that rewrote a gate paid exactly the same, which is to say
# the rule "a changed gate re-proves itself" was enforced by nobody.
# A row says: when one of these paths changes, run these commands. Each job that
# carries a proof runs `gate-self-tests.py plan` as a step of its own and guards
# each command with `steps.<routing step>.outputs.<id> == 'true'`, compared WHOLE.
# NO JOB DEPENDS ON ANOTHER FOR ROUTING, and that is load-bearing rather than
# tidy. Measured on a probe pull request: when a shared routing job failed, the
# jobs needing it were SKIPPED, and a required status check that is skipped
# SATISFIES branch protection -- the pull request reported UNSTABLE, which is
# mergeable, not BLOCKED. Two of the five required contexts here were among them.
# `plan` audits before it plans, so a routing defect reddens the job it would have
# mis-routed, including the required ones. That is what makes the audit blocking;
# the standalone `gate-routing` job is only an early signal.
# The audit refuses more than a missing guard, and the shapes that matter are the
# ones that leave a job GREEN: a guard written `== 'false'`, which inverts the
# routing and reads like routing; a guard naming a step that does not exist or
# sitting above the step that sets it; an `if:` on a job holding a proof; a
# `continue-on-error` letting a red proof pass; and worst, an `if:` on the routing
# STEP, which empties every output in the job and skips the audit along with the
# proofs. `--self-test` carries a named case per shape and that case list, not a
# count in prose, is the enumeration.
# FORMAT: three TAB-separated columns, or four. Blank lines and `#` lines are
# ignored.
#   1  id        [a-z][a-z0-9_]*, unique. It becomes an output of the routing
#                STEP and is read as `steps.<step>.outputs.<id>`, where a hyphen
#                would parse as subtraction.
#   2  commands  comma-separated. Each must appear VERBATIM as one line of a
#                `run:` in .github/workflows/ci.yml, on a step guarded by this
#                row's id. Drift in either direction reddens the audit, so the
#                manifest cannot describe a workflow that has moved on.
#   3  paths     comma-separated, repo-relative, each an existing file. A diff
#                touching any of them runs column 2. On an `always` row this is
#                a single `-`, because such a row routes nothing.
#   4  when      optional. `routed` (the default, and what an omitted column
#                means) or `always`.
# WHAT AN `always` ROW IS FOR, and it is not routing. Some checks read files
# OTHER than their own, so the diffs likeliest to break them never touch them:
# `--release-wiring` reads release.yml and MainDistributionPipeline.yml as
# structure, and `--release-rehearsal` executes the release job's `run:` steps.
# Both run unguarded in `doc-surface` for that reason. Nothing required them to
# be there: deleting both steps left this manifest, the audit, every self-test
# and the comment checker at exit 0, because a step nothing registers is a step
# nothing misses. An `always` row registers the command and the audit then
# requires a step to run it with NO `if:` and no `continue-on-error` -- the
# opposite of what it requires of a routed row, and for the same reason.
# ALWAYS-ON, and deliberately so: this manifest, the router, and the workflow
# itself. A change to any of the three re-runs every gate's self-test, because a
# change to the routing cannot be trusted to route itself.
# WHAT A ROW CANNOT SAY, and it costs a real gap. Column 3 lists FILES, and a
# gate whose detection depends on another module is not covered by watching its
# own file alone: `scripts/check_sample_patterns.py` imports
# `scripts/check_taxonomy_content.py`, so editing the imported module routes
# `taxonomy_content` and NOT `sample_patterns`, whose self-test exercises code it
# no longer re-proves. Add the imported file to the importing row when you notice
# one; nothing here derives it. `extension_stamp` watches
# `.github/scripts/assemble-release-assets.sh` for the same reason: its release
# rehearsal runs that script to produce the asset names its cases are then asked
# about, so a change there changes what those cases exercise.
# THE BOUNDARY. A row belongs here when its command exists to prove a GATE can
# fail. `.github/scripts/test-download-model.sh` and `scripts/test_score_clean_label.sh`
# are tests of a tool rather than proofs of a gate, and `scripts/test_evidence.sh`
# is the evidence suite itself; those keep running on every diff. What is routed
# is the mutation harness that proves the suite detects.
